author: Vincent Augerot
name: HardSlice command slice
description: A command slice of a hardslice-api solution: command, validator, handler, endpoint, validator tests and integration tests, or, with --parameters none, an empty command without validator nor validator tests. --route and --method choose its endpoint. With --endpoint none, a system command that only the application sends, without endpoint nor HTTP test, and with --every <interval> or --daily-at <hh:mm> --time-zone <id>, one that AddRecurringCommand sends at regular intervals or every day, with --retry <delay>x<count> to send it again after a failed cycle and --at-start to send it once when the application starts too. --require <policy> protects its endpoint with an authorization policy of the application, and tests its 401. Run it from the root of the solution with --project src/<App>/<App>.csproj.

Module.description: The module of the slice, in PascalCase, such as Bookings: src/<App>/Features/<Module>/<Module>Module.cs must exist.

Response.description: What the command returns: id (a Guid, by default), none (a bool, false answered with 404) or the PascalCase name of a DTO of values that the slice declares.

Parameters.description: What the command takes from the request: id (a Guid Id to replace with the fields of the use case, checked by a validator, by default) or none (an empty record, without validator: what it needs comes from the database, the configuration or a service of its module). --every implies none.

choices.description: A Guid Id, to replace with the fields of the use case, its validator and its validator tests.
No parameter: an empty record, an endpoint without body, no validator nor validator tests.

Endpoint.description: How the command is sent: http (an endpoint of the module, by default) or none (a system command, which implements ISystemCommand<TResponse>: only a type of its module sends it, such as a hosted service, and HS004 refuses an endpoint for it). --every implies none.

choices.description: An endpoint, mapped on the group of the module, and integration tests that send HTTP requests.
A system command, without endpoint: its integration tests send it through IMediator.

Route.description: The route of the endpoint under the group of the module, chosen after the resource it changes rather than the use case: lowercase words separated by hyphens, and route parameters between braces such as {id:guid}, separated by slashes, such as versions or {id:guid}/extensions, or / for the group itself. The name of the slice in kebab-case by default. With --method DELETE and --parameters id, /{id:guid} follows it.

Method.description: The HTTP method of the endpoint: POST (by default), PUT, PATCH or DELETE, in any case. A DELETE has no body: with --parameters id, it reads the Id of the command from its route, /{id:guid} after --route.

Every.description: Sends the command at regular intervals, through AddRecurringCommand in the module: the interval as [d.]hh:mm:ss, longer than zero and under 49 days, such as 00:00:30 or 1.00:00:00, which the key <Module>:<Name>:Interval of the configuration replaces. --retry sends it again after a failed cycle. Implies --endpoint none and --parameters none: a system command without parameter, whose integration test runs three cycles on a FakeTimeProvider.

Require.description: Protects the endpoint with the authorization policy of that name, which the application registers in Shared/Http with its authentication scheme, such as AdminKey: the endpoint chains .RequireAuthorization("<policy>"), an integration test asserts its 401 without authentication, and the other tests send their requests through app.CreateAuthorizedClient("<policy>"), the client of that policy that AppFactory.AuthorizedClients holds. A name of letters, digits, '.', '_', ':' and '-', starting with a letter. Refused with --endpoint none, --every and --daily-at: a system command has no endpoint.

DailyAt.description: Sends the command every day at that local time, through AddRecurringCommand in the module: hh:mm on 24 hours, such as 04:30, in the time zone of --time-zone, which the keys <Module>:<Name>:DailyAt and <Module>:<Name>:TimeZone of the configuration replace. A time that a change of the clocks skips moves forward by the length of the change, and one that the clocks repeat is sent once. Implies --endpoint none and --parameters none, as --every does, and is refused with it: a system command without parameter, whose integration test runs two days of cycles on a FakeTimeProvider.

TimeZone.description: The time zone of --daily-at, by its IANA id, such as America/Toronto or Europe/Paris: UTC by default. Refused without --daily-at.

Retry.description: Sends the command again after a failed cycle of --every or --daily-at: <delay>x<count>, the delay as [d.]hh:mm:ss, longer than zero and under 49 days, and the count from 1 to 99, such as 01:00:00x3 for three retries an hour apart, which the keys <Module>:<Name>:RetryDelay and <Module>:<Name>:Retries of the configuration replace. A retry that succeeds ends them, and the next instant of the schedule comes after the last one. Its integration test fails a cycle and each retry. Refused without --every or --daily-at.

AtStart.description: Also sends the command of --every or --daily-at once when the application starts, before the first instant of its schedule, such as an import that must not wait for the night: the registration chains AlsoAtStart() to its schedule, which the key <Module>:<Name>:AtStart of the configuration replaces, and an integration test runs the cycle at start at TestInstants.Start. The conditions of the command decide on it as on any cycle (dotnet new hardslice-condition), and --retry sends it again after a failure. Refused without --every or --daily-at.

Accepted.value: (AppIsKnown && NameIsGiven && NameIsPascalCase && !NameHasSuffix && ModuleIsPascalCase && ModuleExists && ResponseIsAccepted && !ResponseNeedsParameters && RouteIsValid && !RouteHidesId && MethodIsAccepted && !EndpointOptionsWithoutEndpoint && !EveryContradictsOptions && EveryIsValid && RequireIsValid && !RequireWithoutEndpoint && DailyAtIsValid && TimeZoneIsValid && RetryIsValid && !EveryWithDailyAt && !DailyAtContradictsOptions && !TimeZoneWithoutDailyAt && !RetryWithoutSchedule && !AtStartWithoutSchedule)

postActions.description: Refuses a solution whose web project it cannot read.

manualInstructions.text: error: hardslice-command reads the application from its web project, which it could not evaluate. Run it from the root of the solution with --project src/<App>/<App>.csproj, once the solution is restored (after a first build or check), such as: dotnet new hardslice-command --project src/<App>/<App>.csproj --module <Module> --name <Name>. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a slice without name.

manualInstructions.text: error: --name is required: the use case in PascalCase, without the Command suffix, such as --name ExtendBooking. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a name that is not PascalCase.

manualInstructions.text: error: --name 'CommandName' is not PascalCase: it names the slice folder, its namespace and its types, such as --name ExtendBooking. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a name with the Command suffix.

manualInstructions.text: error: --name 'CommandName' ends with Command: pass the use case alone, the template names the command <Name>Command. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a module name that is not PascalCase.

manualInstructions.text: error: --module 'ModuleName' is not PascalCase: pass the name of an existing module, such as the folder of src/MyApp/Features/<Module>/. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a module that does not exist.

manualInstructions.text: error: module 'ModuleName' does not exist: src/MyApp/Features/ModuleName/ModuleNameModule.cs was not found. Create the module first with dotnet new hardslice-module --project src/MyApp/MyApp.csproj --name ModuleName, then add the slice. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses an unknown response.

manualInstructions.text: error: --response 'ResponseTypeName' is neither id, none nor the PascalCase name of a DTO, such as --response ExtensionDto. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a DTO named as a type that the slice already uses.

manualInstructions.text: error: --response 'ResponseTypeName' would name the DTO as a type that the slice already uses: Guid is the type of its identifier, and the slice CommandName names its command, handler, validator and endpoint. Name the DTO after what it holds, such as --response CommandNameDto, or pass --response id or --response none. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a command without parameters that answers 404 to an aggregate it cannot name.

manualInstructions.text: error: --response none answers 404 to an unknown aggregate, which a command with --parameters none has no identifier to look for, nor one with --every or --daily-at, which imply it. Pass --response id for the identifier of the aggregate it creates or changes, or the PascalCase name of a DTO of what it did, such as --response ImportResultDto, or keep the parameters with --parameters id. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a route that ASP.NET Core or the tests could not use.

manualInstructions.text: error: --route '/slice-route' is not a route of lowercase words separated by hyphens, and route parameters between braces such as {id:guid}, separated by slashes, such as --route versions or --route {id:guid}/extensions. Pass --route / for the group of the module itself. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a route that already holds the parameter that DELETE appends.

manualInstructions.text: error: --route '/slice-route' holds a parameter id, which --method DELETE appends to it as /{id:guid} to read the Id of the command. Remove it from --route, such as --route versions, or pass / for the group of the module. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses GET, the method of a query.

manualInstructions.text: error: --method GET only reads, while a command changes state: pass --method POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, or generate a query with dotnet new hardslice-query. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses an unknown HTTP method.

manualInstructions.text: error: --method 'HttpMethodName' is not POST, PUT, PATCH or DELETE, the methods of a command, such as --method PUT. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses --route or --method for a system command, which has no endpoint.

manualInstructions.text: error: --endpoint none generates a system command, which only the application sends and which has no endpoint, while --route and --method choose its endpoint. Remove them, or keep the endpoint with --endpoint http. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses an interval that a timer cannot wait.

manualInstructions.text: error: --every 'RecurringInterval' is not an interval of the form [d.]hh:mm:ss, longer than zero and under 49 days, such as --every 00:00:30, --every 01:00:00 or --every 1.00:00:00. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses --every with --parameters id or --endpoint http.

manualInstructions.text: error: --every sends a new command at regular intervals, built without parameter and sent by the application only, so it implies --parameters none and --endpoint none, while --parameters id or --endpoint http asks for the opposite. Remove them, or generate the slice without --every. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a time of day that is not hh:mm.

manualInstructions.text: error: --daily-at 'RecurringDailyAt' is not a time of day of the form hh:mm on 24 hours, such as --daily-at 04:30 or --daily-at 23:00. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a time zone that is not an IANA id.

manualInstructions.text: error: --time-zone is not the IANA id of a time zone, an area and a location separated by a slash such as --time-zone America/Toronto or --time-zone Europe/Paris, or UTC. A Windows name such as Eastern Standard Time is refused. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses retries that are not a delay and a count.

manualInstructions.text: error: --retry 'RecurringRetry' is not <delay>x<count>, the delay as [d.]hh:mm:ss, longer than zero and under 49 days, and the count from 1 to 99, such as --retry 01:00:00x3 for three retries an hour apart. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses --every with --daily-at.

manualInstructions.text: error: --every sends the command at regular intervals and --daily-at every day at a time: pass one of them. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses --daily-at with --parameters id or --endpoint http.

manualInstructions.text: error: --daily-at sends a new command every day, built without parameter and sent by the application only, so it implies --parameters none and --endpoint none, while --parameters id or --endpoint http asks for the opposite. Remove them, or generate the slice without --daily-at. To send a command that keeps its endpoint every day too, generate it without --daily-at and register it with AddRecurringCommand, as the skill add-slice shows. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses --time-zone without --daily-at.

manualInstructions.text: error: --time-zone is the time zone of the time of day of --daily-at, which is missing. Pass --daily-at <hh:mm> with it, or remove it. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses --retry without --every or --daily-at.

manualInstructions.text: error: --retry sends a recurring command again after a failed cycle, while the slice has no schedule: pass --every <interval> or --daily-at <hh:mm> with it, or remove it. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses --at-start without --every or --daily-at.

manualInstructions.text: error: --at-start sends a recurring command once when the application starts too, while the slice has no schedule: pass --every <interval> or --daily-at <hh:mm> with it, or remove it. To send a command that keeps its endpoint at start too, register it with AddRecurringCommand and a RecurringSchedule that chains AlsoAtStart(), as the skill add-slice shows. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses a policy name that the generated code could not hold.

manualInstructions.text: error: --require 'AuthorizationPolicyName' is not the name of an authorization policy that the template can write: letters, digits, '.', '_', ':' and '-', starting with a letter, such as --require AdminKey. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Refuses --require for a system command, which has no endpoint to protect.

manualInstructions.text: error: --require protects the endpoint of the slice with an authorization policy, while --endpoint none, --every and --daily-at generate a system command, which only the application sends and which has no endpoint. Remove --require, or keep the endpoint with --endpoint http and without --every nor --daily-at. Nothing was created.

postActions.description: Lines to add to the module of the slice.

manualInstructions.text:
Register the slice in src/MyApp/Features/ModuleName/ModuleNameModule.cs:
1. Add the usings that the file does not have yet:
using MyApp.Features.ModuleName.CommandName;
using MyApp.Shared.Messaging;
2. In AddModuleNameModule, register the handler by its contract, without validator since the command has no parameter:
            .AddScoped<IRequestHandler<CommandNameCommand, Guid>, CommandNameHandler>()
3. CommandNameCommand is a system command, which has no endpoint: send it from a type of module ModuleName other than its handler and its validator, such as a hosted service in src/MyApp/Features/ModuleName/CommandName/ that creates it and sends it through IMediator in a scope of its own, registered in AddModuleNameModule. HS004 fails the build until a type of the module sends it.
Then complete the slice and its tests: each TODO(hardslice): marker fails the check until it is replaced.

            .AddScoped<IRequestHandler<CommandNameCommand, ResponseTypeName>, CommandNameHandler>()
3. CommandNameCommand is a system command, which has no endpoint: send it from a type of module ModuleName other than its handler and its validator, such as a hosted service in src/MyApp/Features/ModuleName/CommandName/ that creates it and sends it through IMediator in a scope of its own, registered in AddModuleNameModule. HS004 fails the build until a type of the module sends it.
Then complete the slice and its tests: each TODO(hardslice): marker fails the check until it is replaced.

Register the slice in src/MyApp/Features/ModuleName/ModuleNameModule.cs:

using MyApp.Features.ModuleName.CommandName;

2. In AddModuleNameModule, register the handler by its contract, without validator since the command has no parameter, and send the command every day at RecurringDailyAt in RecurringTimeZone, or at ModuleName:CommandName:DailyAt in ModuleName:CommandName:TimeZone of the configuration when they are set:

postActions.description: What the policy of the endpoint asks of the application and of its tests.

manualInstructions.text: The endpoint requires the authorization policy AuthorizationPolicyName, which the application registers in src/MyApp/Shared/Http/ with its authentication scheme (docs/rules/HS015.md). Its integration tests send their requests through app.CreateAuthorizedClient("AuthorizationPolicyName"), which fails until AuthorizedClients, in tests/MyApp.IntegrationTests/AppFactory.cs, holds the client of that policy, and assert its 401 without authentication.
